title: Struggle By Early Nationalists To Secure Press Freedom
definition: The systematic campaign by the Indian National Congress (INC) and early nationalist leaders (1885-1905) to challenge colonial legislative curbs on the press, viewing it as the 'fourth estate' for political education and public opinion mobilization.
importanceInUpsc: Essential for understanding the evolution of Indian nationalism, the role of the press as a tool for mass mobilization, and the colonial state's repressive legislative apparatus.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Struggle By Early Nationalists To Secure Press Freedom.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
prerequisites: Evolution of the Press in India (1780-1857)
Early phase of the Indian National Congress
